stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Guide to all 14 games on a massive hockey Saturday
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
It's Saturday, which means it's time for another super-sized NHL schedule.

This week, there are 14 games from which to choose -- but why choose one, when multi-view exists? Multi-view is even more important Saturday, with a whopping eight games beginning at 7 p.m. ET!

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Seattle Kraken at Carolina Hurricanes

1 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | CAR -325, O/U: 6.5

The final game of the season between the Kraken and Hurricanes (usual caveat: unless they play in the Stanley Cup Final) takes place at Veikkaus Arena in Helsinki, as did their game Thursday.

Carolina won that first game 4-1 -- thanks to two goals from Finland's Sebastian Aho -- so should we expect anything different Saturday?

Shots on goal should be a focus for the Kraken, who managed just 13 of them Thursday, compared with 30 for the Canes.

Seattle could also consider a goaltending switch from Philipp Grubauer to Joey Daccord, although the latter has struggled a bit to start the season by his own lofty standards.

Winnipeg Jets at Chicago Blackhawks

3:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WPG -155, O/U: 6.5

The Jets are on a heater. Beginning with their record-setting comeback against the Canadiens on Nov. 3, they have won five straight games, with an aggregate score of 27-14.

On the other side, the Blackhawks are coming off a victory, just their fifth of the season.

The matchup appears a little one-sided, but the Blackhawks won the first matchup in the season series; Artyom Levshunov scored the winning goal in OT to send the United Center fans home happy. Will this game also be close?

Minnesota Wild at Boston Bruins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -122, O/U: 6.5

Though it's not quite a showdown between division leaders -- Boston fell behind Tampa and Montreal on Thursday -- this is clearly Saturday's marquee matchup, as two legit Cup contenders square off for the final time (until, possibly the Cup Final).

The Wild won the first matchup of the season 4-1 in the Twin Cities as Kirill Kaprizov scored two goals, and Quinn Hughes added another. That was more than enough for Jesper Wallstedt, who stopped 26 of 27 shots on goal.

This time, the game is in Boston, and it's expected that Jeremy Swayman will get the nod in the B's crease opposite Wallstedt.

Can David Pastrnak and his teammates score more than one versus the "Wall of St. Paul" this time?

Edmonton Oilers at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | EDM -155, O/U: 6.5

One of the greatest players to come out of the Greater Toronto Area (well, one of the best to come out of any area) returns. What kind of a show will Connor McDavid put on for the crowd at Scotiabank Arena?

In his past four games in Toronto, McDavid has four goals and seven assists. That kind of output would help his quest for 200 points this season -- and the Oilers' fate in this contest, as the Leafs won 7-2 in Edmonton on Oct. 24.

That game was the William Nylander show, as the veteran winger finished with two goals, while Anthony Stolarz stopped 30 of 32 shots.

Colorado Avalanche at Montreal Canadiens

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MTL -118, O/U: 6.5

Consider this the matchup right underneath the marquee Wild-Bruins tilt, between two clubs that have a lot in common:

Patrick Roy won a Stanley Cup with each team
Each made the 2026 playoffs and looks to be a strong bet to do so again in 2027
Both teams beat the Maple Leafs within the past week

This will be the first showdown between them in 2026-27. Will we look back on it Saturday night as a Nathan MacKinnon-dominated game, or will it be a party for the home team led by Cole Caufield and Lane Hutson?

Detroit Red Wings at Tampa Bay Lightning

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -225, O/U: 6.5

There are some similarities between these teams as well, most notably that a key player on each team has requested a trade.

In Tampa's case, Nikita Kucherov is still playing -- and playing extraordinarily well, leading the team with 28 points. In Detroit's case, Dylan Larkin is no longer playing after a brief return in October.

The Lightning overwhelmed the Red Wings 4-2 in their opening matchup this season. Does this contest play out differently?

Ottawa Senators at Pittsburgh Penguins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -125, O/U: 6.5

Both of these teams were sent home after the first round of the 2026 playoffs, but their fortunes since could not be more different.

The Sens had a roller coaster of an offseason, trading Brady Tkachuk to Florida, using one of the picks acquired in that deal to add William Eklund, then racing out to a 12-6-2 start that has them squarely in the playoff picture.

The Pens didn't do much this offseason, and have wobbled to a 7-10-2 start that has fans wondering if this is the season any of the star veterans will be traded if things don't turn around quickly.

New Jersey Devils at Washington Capitals

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -115, O/U: 6.5

For the second time in three days, these two Metro powers will square off; this time in the nation's capital after a 5-2 Devils win in Newark on Thursday.

The teams seemed to trade momentum in that contest, and the score was justly tied 2-2 after two periods. New Jersey's Vladislav Kolyachonok scored the go-ahead goal early in the third, and Stefan Noesen and Jack Hughes added insurance.

Also of note: The win for Connor Hellebuyck runs his record to 6-0-0 following his trade from the Jets. Also also of note: It has now been over a month since Alex Ovechkin scored a goal.

After this showdown, the two teams won't play again until Jan. 24. Who gets the upper hand, with both looking like legit contenders for playoff spots?

Philadelphia Flyers at Columbus Blue Jackets

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CBJ -142, O/U: 5.5

Just like the Red Wings-Lightning matchup, there's a high-profile player on each team who has requested a trade/shown interest in new scenery on each of these teams.

Though Matvei Michkov's status is a bit more confusing based on what was reported this week, his production is not. He leads Philly in points (15) and goals (10).

Zach Werenski was almost traded this offseason before he nixed a deal to the Stars, and he is back doing what he always does: leading the Jackets in assists (12), and being among the NHL league leaders in average ice time (28:09 per game, second to only Quinn Hughes).

The game is a battle between the seventh and eighth seeds in the Metro, both of whom need points any way they can get them to avoid falling out of the picture before December.

Florida Panthers at St. Louis Blues

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -115, O/U: 6.5

The Tkachuk Bros have history in St. Louis -- having been raised in the area -- and Matthew was photographed posing behind bars with the Cup in Brentwood, Missouri, in 2025.

So it's a homecoming of sorts for the family, but Matthew and Brady won't be playing nicely against their Missouri hosts.

Matthew is the Panthers' scoring leader, with 28 points, and the Blues are led in points (14) and goals (10) by Jimmy Snuggerud. But the real star of St. Louis' season thus far is goaltender Joel Hofer, who is seventh in the NHL in goals-against average (2.15) and tied for third in save percentage (.926).

Buffalo Sabres at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -142, O/U: 6.5

Buffalo sports fans have long memories, so the 1999 Cup Final still brings up bad memories for those who experienced it. The Sabres didn't do much to dispel those bad memories in these two teams' prior meeting on Oct. 8, losing 4-0 at home.

The Stars had four goal scorers in that one, although their scoring in general has been a bit top-heavy; just six players have double-digit points, led by Mikko Rantanen (21) and Jason Robertson (20).

The Sabres have eight players who have 10 points or more, but that scoring balance won't matter much if no one can put a puck past Jake Oettinger again.

San Jose Sharks at Utah Mammoth

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -205, O/U: 6.5

Both of these teams leveled up in 2026-27, as the Mammoth made the playoffs, and the Sharks narrowly missed. It was anticipated that both would challenge for a postseason spot again, but only one of them appears to be playing along -- and just barely.

As play begins Saturday, the Mammoth are in the second Western wild-card spot, and the Sharks are four points back (and with three teams in the way).

The stakes are clear. Which group of young offensive talent can shine brighter in this critical spotlight?

New York Islanders at Anaheim Ducks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | ANA -115, O/U: 6.5

Though the Sharks and Mammoth are having issues, the Ducks seem to have taken flight (a loss to the Preds on Wednesday notwithstanding). Anaheim enters this matchup third in the Pacific with 21 points, looking to bolster that position.

On the other side, the Isles are tied with the Capitals with 20 points (albeit in one more game than Washington), and it's not outlandish to think they'll stick in the playoff picture until season's end.

Two critical points are on the line in the second and final showdown between these teams this season; the Isles won the first 3-2 on Long Island on Oct. 20.

Calgary Flames at Los Angeles Kings

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | LA -175, O/U: 5.5

The irresistible force meets the unmovable object! Or, something like that.

These two are in the bottom eight in preventing goals; the Flames are tied for 24th at 3.47 goals allowed per game, while the Kings are 28th at 3.53. So, lots of goals in this one, right?

Maybe not. Both teams are in the bottom seven in scoring goals; the Kings are 26th at 2.76 goals per game, and the Flames are 28th at 2.47.

Which side blinks first?

Reminder: Fans can catch all the action in the NHL streaming hub and on the ESPN App.

Today in hockey history
No matter what era, 1,000 points in the NHL is massive. And on this date, two quite prominent players hit that milestone.

First up was Brett Hull on Nov. 14, 1998. While playing for the Dallas Stars, Hull scored the milestone point in a 3-1 win over the Boston Bruins in his 815th career game.

Then, on Nov. 14, 2024, Connor McDavid joined the 1,000-point club to lead the Edmonton Oilers to a 3-2 win over the Predators. It was Connor's 659th game.

Though achieving the feat in 659 games is quite impressive, it is the fourth fastest in history. The players to hit 1,000 points quicker than McDavid? Wayne Gretzky (424 games), Mario Lemieux (513) and Mike Bossy (656).

stories.headline: NFL Week 10 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
stories.summary: Touchdown for Chuba Hubbard? Fantasy upside for Aaron Rodgers? Trick play from the Raiders? Let's predict 15 things for Week 10.
stories.byline: Matt Bowen, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody, Ben Solak and Seth Walder
stories.body:
Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Commanders beat the Giants on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Will the Steelers upset the Bengals? How many yards will Trey McBride have against the Rams? Could Jadarian Price score his first NFL touchdown? And will Raiders coach Klint Kubiak dial up a trick play in Fernando Mendoza's first start?

Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Carolina Panthers +2.5 (+110 moneyline) at New Orleans Saints

Quarterback Bryce Young is getting the ball out more quickly recently without sacrificing chances downfield, which could be helpful against New Orleans' pass rush. The Saints are allowing 7.8 yards per pass attempt, giving Tetairoa McMillan opportunities to make big plays.

New Orleans hasn't gotten much from its running game, and it will be without starting center Erik McCoy (biceps injury) on Sunday. That puts more stress on quarterback Tyler Shough, enabling Carolina to keep this close and potentially win outright.

Pittsburgh Steelers +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Cincinnati Bengals

Running back Jaylen Warren gives Pittsburgh a way to control this game. He already piled up 176 total yards in Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over Cincinnati, and the Bengals keep giving up long runs this season.

Cincinnati also struggles to defend the middle of the field, where Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has strong options in WR Germie Bernard and TE Darnell Washington. Bengals QB Joe Burrow will get his points, but Pittsburgh can answer without asking Rodgers to force deep throws.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Malik Washington, WR, Miami Dolphins: 11 targets, 7 receptions, 78 receiving yards, 1 touchdown

Every year I look for the players who are excelling in ESPN's open score -- which measures a receiver's ability to get open on all routes, regardless of target -- but struggling in catch score. That's because open score is much more stable than catch score and correlates better with future production.

Washington fits this profile exactly with an 82 open score (tied with Garrett Wilson for second best) but just a 38 catch score (below average). So there is a decent chance Washington's production will increase, and it could happen as early as this Sunday -- even with backup quarterback Kyle McCord throwing him the ball. Washington should line up against Colts nickel cornerback Justin Walley, who missed the past two games with a knee injury and is allowing 1.8 yards per coverage snap, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That's well above the 1.1 average.

Trey McBride, TE, Arizona Cardinals: 13 targets, 9 receptions, 99 receiving yards

If I were quarterback Carson Beck, I would make a point of throwing to McBride when in doubt during my NFL debut. But that would be especially true now that Michael Wilson is out for the season with a neck injury. And even further because 23% of targets against the Rams' defense have been to tight ends, the sixth-highest rate in the league.

As long as cornerback Trent McDuffie isn't on McBride, he ought to be the priority target on most plays. If the Cardinals fall behind, McBride should be in line for quite a bit of garbage-time production to come close to the 100-yard mark.

Justin Eboigbe, DT, Los Angeles Chargers: 1.0 sacks, 4 pressures, 19% pass rush win rate

Eboigbe recorded 6.0 sacks a year ago but has just 0.5 this season. Plus, he has a well-below-average pass rush win rate. So why am I forecasting a big game for Eboigbe on Monday? Because of who he'll line up against. Ravens right guard John Simpson has a sixth-percentile pass block win rate at the position, while center Cam Jurgens is literally last in pass block win rate at his position since he started playing for the Ravens in Week 7.

Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers

Aaron Rodgers, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers (35.4% rostered in ESPN leagues)

Rodgers has averaged just 8.9 fantasy points over his past two games, with Pittsburgh leaning heavily on its running game. That could change Sunday night against a Bengals offense that ranks second in points per game, which could force the Steelers to throw more to keep pace.

Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdown passes against Cincinnati in Week 3, finishing with 22.6 fantasy points. The Bengals have also allowed 17.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

Corey Kiner, RB, New England Patriots (31.9%)

Kiner could lead the Patriots' backfield against the Lions this week, with Rhamondre Stevenson listed as questionable (knee tendon issue) and TreVeyon Henderson is out. Kiner rushed for 55 yards and a touchdown on eight carries against the Packers last week; he leads New England with 4.9 yards per carry this season.

Detroit has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs, so it's a tough matchup. But Kiner could see 14-plus rushing attempts, while Lan Larison handles more of the work on passing downs.

Tutu Atwell, WR, Los Angeles Rams (8.1%)

With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both sidelined, Atwell could see a lot more targets against the Cardinals. He has drawn nine targets over his past two games and played more snaps than any other healthy Rams receiver against the Commanders.

Arizona has allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers and the second-most passing touchdowns in the league. Atwell's production has been inconsistent, but his ability to make plays downfield and the opportunity for more targets make him worth considering in deeper leagues.

Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers

Jadarian Price, RB, Seattle Seahawks

Price had 78 total yards in the Week 9 win over the Cardinals, and he looked explosive in the pass game with four receptions for 54 yards. He will continue to split touches with Zach Charbonnet on Sunday versus the Raiders, but I see him scoring his first pro touchdown here -- off a screen pass.

George Kittle, TE, San Francisco 49ers

Take the target volume with Kittle, plus the prime matchup versus the Dallas defense. Kittle has seen at least seven targets in three straight games, and coach Kyle Shanahan can scheme up his tight end to press the seams against the Cowboys' split-safety coverages.

I'd expect multiple red zone targets for Kittle on Sunday. And the 49ers are the best in the league at turning those targets into touchdowns (84.6% red zone touchdown percentage this season).

Chuba Hubbard, RB, Carolina Panthers

Hubbard has at least one rushing score in three of his past five games, and he is seeing consistent volume with 20 or more touches in four contests. Meanwhile, the Saints are giving up 133.9 rushing yards per game (fourth most) and have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns this season (tied for second most). With steady volume and red zone touches, Hubbard could easily find the end zone Sunday.

Solak makes four more predictions

Rams WR CJ Daniels will score a touchdown

The Rams' undrafted free agent receiver is in line for his first NFL action now that Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all on IR. Daniels critically has something that projected starting receivers Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell lack: size. At 6-foot-2, 205 pounds, don't be surprised if Daniels sees third-down and red zone usage against the Cardinals.

There will be four combined missed field goals in Chiefs-Falcons

The Chiefs are rolling with Harrison Butker for another week despite his 12-for-19 start on field goal attempts -- he's 6-for-13 on anything 40-plus yards. Meanwhile, the Falcons signed Jake Moody off the Ravens' practice squad following the release of Nick Folk (13-for-18). I'm rooting for some fourth-and-longs at the 37-yard line that force long field goal tries.

The Raiders will score on a trick play

I think Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak will have some good schematic tricks up his sleeve for the Seahawks' defense after watching it all of last season as Seattle's offensive coordinator. Is there a particular defender he knows will be too aggressive against a double pass? Or lose contain on a reverse?

In quarterback Fernando Mendoza's first start, the Raiders need to manufacture explosive gains with creative playcalling. And well-timed red zone trickery could do just that.

Bills QB Josh Allen and Jets QB Geno Smith will combine for 600 passing yards

The Jets are 2-7 and held pat at the trade deadline. Coach Aaron Glenn knows he needs emphatic wins down the stretch of the 2026 season to hold onto his job, and that's especially true in a division where he's 0-8 since he took over.

I think the Jets can come out with a strong effort at home Sunday against a Buffalo secondary that is still gettable in coverage after enjoying a couple of easy offenses (Vikings and Ravens). The potential for a shootout is high in this one.

stories.headline: Sources: San Jose Earthquakes sold for $625 million to Heath Freeman
stories.summary: Alden Global Capital co-founder Heath Freeman is purchasing the San Jose Earthquakes from John Fisher, following MLS owners' approval of the sale Thursday.
stories.body:
The San Jose Earthquakes announced that Alden Global Capital co-founder Heath Freeman will acquire the team, as well as the club's home venue, PayPal Park, from John Fisher.

Sources confirmed a report from Sportico that the sale reflects an enterprise value of $625 million. The MLS board of governors unanimously approved the transfer of ownership Thursday, noting that the transaction will close in the coming weeks.

The deal will complete a lengthy sales process that began in June 2025. Investment bank Moelis helped facilitate the deal.

"My family and I are honored and humbled to be the next generation owners of the San Jose Earthquakes. I would like to thank John Fisher and the Fisher family for their confidence in me. I know how much they love this team and we expect to continue making them proud in this new era of the Quakes," Freeman said.

"Our vision is simple - winning on and off the field for San Jose and the entire region. The Bay Area is home to some of the world's great institutions, sports franchises and leaders. The standard has been set. We are eager to partner with and connect our community more closely with the Earthquakes and immerse them in our world."

The Quakes struggled during much of Fisher's tenure as owner, reaching the postseason just four times in the past 11 seasons. This season, under manager Bruce Arena, San Jose is in the MLS Cup Playoffs. It will face Houston Dynamo FC in Round 1 when it hosts Game 1 of the best-of-three series Nov. 24 at PayPal Park. The club won the 2012 Supporters' Shield.

"We are committed to investing in the team and building a club that consistently competes for championships," Freeman said. "Off the field, we are equally focused on strengthening our connections with fans and communities in San Jose and throughout the Bay Area. We believe the future of the Earthquakes is incredibly bright, and we can't wait to get started and take the Quakes to unforeseen heights."

Freeman has served as president of Alden Global Capital since 2014. He currently serves as chairman of Tribune Enterprises LLC, which owns and manages newspapers including the Chicago Tribune and South Florida Sun Sentinel, and as vice chairman of MNG Enterprises Inc., which manages newspapers such as The Denver Post, the Mercury News and the Boston Herald. Alden Global Capital has recently enacted deep cost cuts across its publications, leading to multiple layoffs.

Fisher has owned the Earthquakes since 2007, when he and Lew Wolff purchased an expansion team to replace the side that relocated to Houston after the 2005 season. During his tenure, he privately financed the construction of PayPal Park.

"My family and I have loved owning this club for almost 20 years and we are extremely grateful for the support of our amazing fans as well as the hard work of all of our coaches, players and staff," Fisher said. "We would like to thank Jared Shawlee and the executive staff for their leadership and the entire Quakes front office for their commitment to the club, the fans and the community."

"I want to thank John Fisher and his family for their nearly two decades of commitment to the San Jose Earthquakes, Major League Soccer and the Bay Area soccer community," said MLS commissioner Don Garber.

"John has been a great partner and a good friend, and his leadership and investment helped build a strong foundation for the club. Heath Freeman is an ambitious owner with a strong belief in the Earthquakes and the Bay Area as one of the country's great soccer markets. We are excited to welcome him to MLS and look forward to the energy and vision he will bring to this next chapter of the club."

Two MLS teams remain on the market. The Saputo family announced plans to sell CF Montréal earlier this week. The Vancouver Whitecaps are also still on the market, with Goldman Sachs leading that process.

BMO Capital Markets is managing the CF Montréal sale as lead financial adviser, with National Bank of Canada Capital Markets as co-adviser.

stories.headline: Six from Team Nurmagomedov, eight in all get prison time over Dvalishvili brawl
stories.summary: Six members of Usman Nurmagomedov's team and two people who filmed the hotel fight also involving Merab Dvalishvili have been handed six-month prison sentences in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
Six members of Team Nurmagomedov have been sentenced to six months in prison following a brawl involving former UFC champion Merab Dvalishvili in an Abu Dhabi hotel.

On Wednesday at the host hotel of a Real American Fighting event, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, the cousin of retired MMA legend Khabib Nurmagomedov, approached Dvalishvili from behind and slapped him, triggering a larger altercation between members of the two camps.

Police arrested and detained all parties. Dvalishvili was later released, according to RAF CEO Chad Bronstein.

According to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, six members of Nurmagomedov's team were each sentenced to six months in prison, fined 300,000 AED (approximately $81,700) and ordered to be deported after serving their sentences. According to The National news outlet in the United Arab Emirates, Dvalishvili and a friend were fined 50,000 AED (approximately $13,600) for "disturbing public security and assaulting others."

Two individuals who filmed the altercation also received six-month prison sentences, according to The National, for violating privacy laws by filming and publishing footage of the incident. The court confiscated their phones to delete footage.

Dvalishvili addressed the incident in a social media post Friday, confirming he was released and writing that he is "good, healthy and ready to go." He added that he was hoping everyone involved in the altercation would be released.

Tensions have escalated between Dvalishvili and Team Nurmagomedov since Dvalishvili defeated Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, in a UFC bantamweight title fight in January 2025. The two camps had another, smaller altercation at an RAF event in the nation of Georgia in July.

Umar Nurmagomedov was scheduled to wrestle former UFC champion Urijah Faber at the RAF event Saturday but has been replaced by Dvalishvili's 21-year-old Georgian friend Saba Lazishvili, who was involved in the hotel brawl Wednesday. Dvalishvili will still compete in his scheduled bout against former UFC champion Marlon Moraes.

Usman Nurmagomedov, 28, recently fought out his exclusive contract with the PFL, and there had been speculation around the possibility of the undefeated fighter signing with the UFC.

UFC CEO Dana White commented on the brawl Thursday during a news conference in New York.

"What a bunch of f---ing idiots," White said. "It's absolutely ridiculous and stupid, and they're all in jail. That is not a place to go f--- around."

stories.headline: Despite injury and illness, Gus Teixeira is still one of this year's top prospects
stories.summary: Gus Teixeira spent much of his top-age year battling injury and illness, but still found a way to be in contention to be the top pick in the open pool, writes Japser Chellappah.
stories.body:
Gustavo Teixeira had a brilliant top-age campaign. He's worked his way into pick 1 conversations, and is locked into the first handful of selections on draft night.

His success is made all the more impressive considering what's played out behind the scenes.

"I had the ankle injury at the start of the year in the first praccy game," Teixeira tells ESPN.

"It was kind of a bit annoying because every week I thought I'd be playing but it just got pushed back. I had the calf injury, I was out for five or six weeks. I rehabbed that, played a game and then the foot pulled up sore and that's why I'm not testing [at the AFL Draft combine].

"I've also been sick for basically the whole year with a virus."

Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder, played valiantly through glandular fever-like symptoms that didn't get diagnosed until the conclusion of the National Championships.

He was playing games deep in the forward 50 but still finding himself short of breath and unable to hit top gear. After being diagnosed with a severe iron deficiency and receiving an infusion he felt the energy he'd been lacking return, but not before a calf injury linked to his virus took Teixeira out for all but one game in the back half of the season.

Most top-10 chances at the AFL Draft thrive off injury-free seasons where they can continually put their name up in lights. Teixeira couldn't do that this year, so he made his moments count.

His first game back from an ankle concern was in a Vic Metro trial game where he showed his worth, kicking two goals from 20 disposals in a best afield display.

"It was a good day out, I was pretty happy with that. It was annoying I couldn't do a bit more of that throughout the year but I'm sure I can do that in the future."

Teixeira had locked himself into Metro's National Championships outfit by halftime, showing off the power and class that recruiters covet.

At the National Championships he was playing under duress from his undiagnosed virus, but he still took the opportunity to show his value deep in attack.

"Obviously I was sick so I was resting a bit, I was sore the first week and they wanted me to play more forward. I kicked a few goals and they wanted me to stay down forward and that's where I was able to impact the most," he tells ESPN.

Teixeira claimed All-Australian honours, booting seven goals in his four outings including a best on ground demolition of the Allies where he kicked four goals from 22 touches.

It was an element of his game that proved his worth outside of the centre square. Teixeira got to dangerous spots and created separation with proactive running, and from there was able to demonstrate his cleanliness and class to make his chances count.

"I've always thought I want to be a midfielder, I want to play in there. Skills are very important as a midfielder so you've got to be clean and you've got to be able to kick. I'm just chipping away at it and improving."

Teixeira is of Brazilian descent via his father Matt, who was born in the city of Belo Horizonte before moving to Australia when he was 25.

He brings Gus back to Brazil every year, and that connection to a non-English speaking country would allow Teixeira to join zoned club St Kilda's Next Generation Academy if not for friction points within the AFL's own NGA rules.

"Belo Horizonte is just inland of Rio... It's like the size of Melbourne but no one's really heard of it. It's a fully different culture and it's always great to go back," he explains.

"The AFL changed the rules for the regions this year, so they allow South American people this year but you need to be in it for three years. I would've only been in it for a year... my younger siblings are in it now. I've got a brother, Eddie, who's 12 and my sister Lucy who's 14."

Like a host of the top prospects this year, Teixeira has been an Essendon supporter his whole life. The Bombers have the top pick and Teixeira is within that bracket of the pool.

"I haven't thought about the Bombers pick-wise, but just the club and thinking about what it would be like obviously going to the Bombers, it'd be great at the moment. They're getting in some good coaches and they've got some good players coming through.

"Really though I'd be stoked to get drafted to any club, moving interstate would be a pretty cool experience. I'm always trying to get the best out of myself, I've always tried to be the best at everything and just put my best foot forward so I'll do that anywhere."

ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
stories.summary: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
stories.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.

That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings. Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

"I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days -- like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

"We believe the return gives us a meaningful opportunity to strengthen this roster over time," a team source said. "That does not mean Jessie stopped being an outstanding player. We are giving up something valuable and we understand that."

On the other hand, the Falcons are in one of the most unique positions in the NFL. Their record is ugly, but they are a half-game out of first place in a weak NFC South. All four teams in the division are sitting at three wins apiece. Atlanta finishes its season playing its NFC South rivals back-to-back-to-back.

So, there was also an argument for standing pat and making a good-faith run at the playoffs, where the Falcons have not been since 2017. Only the New York Jets have a longer drought.

"We're still in it," quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. "... We're so close in a lot of areas and I feel like in this organization we view that a lot. We use that a lot. We are so close.

"I truly believe we have the team and the guys that's going to rally and flip the script because we got a lot of guys that care. Obviously, I feel like matchup wise, I feel like our team is one of the top teams in the league."

The Falcons have shown glimpses of that, such as last month when they toppled the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers in an impressive performance. But since then, they have fallen to the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a full-on downpour and lost to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid.

The schedule does not get any easier. The Kansas City Chiefs will come to town Sunday. After that, the Falcons have their bye week followed by a road game against the Minnesota Vikings, a home game against the Detroit Lions and then a trip to Cleveland. Those teams have a combined 23-10 record.

It will be up to the team's leadership to keep the players focused on the task at hand. ESPN's FPI is giving the Falcons only a 4.5% chance of making the playoffs, but the division remains wide open. The other three teams don't have easy schedules, either.

Left tackle Jake Matthews, the longest-tenured Falcon and the only player left from the 2016 Super Bowl team, said Atlanta had a "really good practice" Wednesday "because everyone was kind of dialed in to 'Hey, this is our objective still and we fully expect to go out and play every weekend to win.'"

"I think [Stefanski's] message and the point was kind of driven home that there's so much still ahead of us this season," Matthews said. "We need to double down."

stories.headline: Messi to play in Argentina Jan. 19 for Inter Miami-River friendly
stories.summary: Lionel Messi will return to play at Estadio Monumental on Jan. 19 when Inter Miami travel to Buenos Aires to play River Plate.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will return to play at Estadio Monumental on Jan. 19 for the first time since his Argentina farewell when Inter Miami travels to Buenos Aires to play River Plate in a friendly.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner has played a total of 29 matches for Argentina at El Monumental, the most recent on Oct. 6 in his national team farewell, where he played his 208th and final game for Argentina.

That match ended with his 126th goal capping a 21-year career for the legendary No. 10, which included two Copa América titles and a World Cup.

This game will mark the first time Messi has played a club match in his home country.

Over his career he has face Argentina clubs four times, including beating Estudiantes with Barcelona at the 2009 Club World Cup in United Arab Emirates and again when Barcelona defeated River for the 2015 Club World Cup in Japan.

Messi has also played two other friendlies vs. Argentina clubs: In 2018 with Barcelona beating Boca Juniors for the Joan Gamper trophy and a friendly in 2024 vs. his boyhood club, Newell's in Miami, which ended in a 1-1 draw.

River Plate is one of South America's most successful clubs, boasting 38 domestic titles and four Copa Libertadores trophies.

Earlier this week, Messi was named a finalist for the 2026 Major League Soccer MVP award. The Inter Miami captain seeks to become the first player to win the prize on three consecutive occasions.

Messi already clinched a record second straight Golden Boot award after scoring 26 goals in the 2026 regular season.

Miami said they expect Messi to be joined by Casemiro, Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez, Nicolás Otamendi and Thiago Almada for the trip.

Inter Miami's previous preseason tours have included visits to Peru, Ecuador, Colombia and Puerto Rico.

Inter Miami will kick off the 2027 Major League Soccer season on Feb. 19 against FC Cincinnati at Nu Stadium.

stories.headline: UFC 334 preview, picks for Ciryl Gane-Josh Hokit and Kayla Harrison-Amanda Nunes
stories.summary: A look at the matchups and experts' picks for both title fights at UFC 334 in New York City.
stories.body:
One year ago, Josh Hokit was virtually unknown in the fight world. On Saturday, he will headline a UFC event at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. One of the biggest questions surrounding him is how much of his soul he's sacrificed to get here. This weekend could provide an answer to an even bigger question.

Hokit (10-0) will challenge heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane (14-2) at UFC 334 (Paramount+, 9 p.m. ET). Hokit, 28, has been one of the sport's biggest breakouts in 2026, thanks in no small part to the controversy he's stirred on the mic. He stood on the South Lawn of the White House in June and made vulgar remarks about former first lady Michelle Obama. He made distasteful 9/11 jokes on social media the same day of the 25th anniversary of the attacks on the very city where he will compete this weekend.

A former collegiate football player at Fresno State University, Hokit has broken character on numerous occasions and said he doesn't even enjoy the attention. But he's using hate and controversy to stand out, and he won't apologize for it. He acknowledged as much again this week, during media appearances in New York.

"I'll never look back and regret it," Hokit said. "I'm here to be remembered. If I have to crack a few eggs to make an omelette, f--- it. If I have to burn the bridge to light the way, f--- it."

Some of Hokit's appalling comments have prompted UFC CEO Dana White to say during an episode of "The Jim Rome Show" on Nov. 4 that he's given Hokit difficult matchups on his way up and that he doesn't like "anything Josh Hokit says." Hokit has taken advantage of the high-profile opportunities he has received this year from White, who's said Hokit earned his title shot on Saturday.

Whether Hokit would tone down his act if he captures a UFC championship -- or double down on it -- remains to be seen. Either way, it does create an intriguing industry-wide storyline to watch on Saturday.

Those who have been offended by Hokit's tactics likely want to see him lose. Such is the effect of him playing a villain.

But there's another reason critics should fear a Hokit victory: It could inspire other fighters to follow his blueprint for success. That could happen, actually, regardless of Saturday's outcome.

More storylines to watch

After 8 years, Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes finally settle their differences

From the moment Harrison walked into the American Top Team gym in South Florida in 2018 to begin her MMA career, she and Nunes were on a path to one of the greatest rivalries in women's MMA -- even if it took years for them to call it one.

The history behind the matchup is as compelling as their individual achievements. Harrison says she wanted to build something in the gym alongside Nunes, while Nunes -- already UFC champion when Harrison arrived -- says she recognized from the start that Harrison wanted to take her place in the sport. Those conflicting perceptions created the tension that led to Saturday's bout, with Nunes coming out of a 3½-year retirement to challenge for Harrison's bantamweight belt.

The fight was originally scheduled for January 2026, but Harrison was forced to withdraw just weeks before the bout to undergo two-level spinal fusion surgery for a neck injury she had been dealing with for years.

Stephen 'Wonderboy' Thompson retirement

Thompson was never the only "nice guy" in MMA, but he might have perfected it more than anyone else.

Thompson has announced that Saturday's bout against Charles Radtke will be the end of his 14-year UFC career. It's fitting that his last act will take place in Madison Square Garden, the same building in which his career could have taken a very different path. Thompson fought Tyron Woodley to a majority draw in November 2016 at UFC 205, the promotion's first event in New York City. He came within one round on one judge's scorecard of becoming UFC champion. Thompson lost an immediate rematch to Woodley in 2017, and never returned to title contention after a 2019 loss to Anthony Pettis.

Nevertheless, Thompson left his mark in the sport. He's regarded as one of the most honorable fighters of the past decade. A karate-based welterweight, Thompson continued teaching children's martial arts classes even as an active, ranked fighter in the UFC. His iconic walkouts to Tenacious D's "Wonderboy" and notable wins over Johny Hendricks, Rory MacDonald, Jorge Masvidal and Robert Whittaker will not soon be forgotten.

"I want to leave this sport knowing that, hey, you can still be at the top of the game and be the good guy," Thompson said. "That's a breath of fresh air. You don't have to be the guy to talk trash all the time."

Coaches' questions and predictions for the title fights

Editor's note: Responses have been edited for brevity and clarity.

Ciryl Gane (c) vs. Josh Hokit

How will Hokit handle Gane's size?

I was in Francis Ngannou's corner against Gane, and the first thing I said was, "This is a big f---ing guy who can move." Hokit is smaller, and could probably be a light heavyweight. He needs to wrestle in this fight, and what will grappling a big guy like that do to his gas tank? Gane's stance switches on the feet are big, because they change the wrestling picture. He's always changing his lead leg, which could force Josh to constantly recalculate where his attacks are. Gane will need to mix in anti-wrestling strikes, meaning target some strikes to the chest and body to negate Josh's level changes. Hokit has to cut off the cage and, once he does get Gane down, prioritize controlling his legs to slow the process of him getting back up. I think the size is a real factor, so I'm picking Gane. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

Can Hokit's chaos disrupt the technical superiority of Gane?

This is Hokit's biggest step up, a true test of the elite -- whereas, I do not believe this is the best guy Gane has fought. The question is whether Hokit's off-the-wall pressure, all the s--- he does in there to make it chaotic, can hold up against a technical fighter like Gane. You have to let Hokit do the things that have gotten him to this point. You don't want him to be sloppy, but I wouldn't try to tighten things up too much. I feel like Gane is going to be too much, though, and expose what Hokit is missing technically. Hokit has to make the fight ugly. I feel Gane is too crisp, too clean, and ends up sparking him. Gane by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Kayla Harrison (c) vs. Amanda Nunes
What do the fighters know that we don't, and how will they use it?

Who got the better of whom in the gym? What do they know intimately about each other that we don't, and how will they use that information? For Amanda, she needs to intercept Kayla's pressure with straight punches. Looping punches allow Kayla to sit down and get into the hips, so those punches scare me. Amanda has to defend the second and third takedown attempts and, if and when she does get taken down, she has to make Kayla work. The issue there is that Amanda has been notorious for her own failed cardio, but she has to make Kayla work for any grappling success. And for Kayla, she can't fight a la carte, which she has done in the past. She can't say, "Now I'm striking; OK, now I'm wrestling." She has to throw strikes to close distance and then blend her wrestling. Prioritize positions over going for submissions and make this a physical fight. I'm going to pick Amanda. I think she wins a decision. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

How will Nunes look after 3½ years away from the Octagon?

Is Nunes still Nunes? Usually in MMA, time off doesn't result in a better, sharper fighter. But Amanda was so dominant and such a beast. I know Amanda personally and I know she wouldn't be coming back if she didn't know she's still got it. I think she will have a good night at the office. It's the power. She has that rare power that can change the outcome of a fight if she hits you just one time. And she's dealt with the pressure that Kayla is going to bring. I know Julianna Peña got Amanda off her game when she beat her in 2021, but I think Amanda went into that fight injured and not caring as much. As long as that's not the case and she comes in ready, just needs to make contact once. Nunes by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Over the past five years the first round has averaged out to 25 selections accounting for father-son and academy bids, but clubs are expecting a number closer to the traditional 18 picks in the final intake of the 18-team competition.

Stricter stipulations around matching bids is at play, with clubs only able to use a maximum of two selections when matching for a club-tied prospect, meaning the selections of Port Adelaide, Carlton, Brisbane and GWS will be absorbed as early bids are matched.

We could see a record number of Indigenous talents picked in the first round. The high-water mark was four in 2005 and 2014, and all of Cochrane, Walker, Caylen Murray (Lions Academy), Toby Krasna and Jake Eime could be taken in the first round in 2026.
